Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

double verb

make or become twice as great

also double in size, redouble, be doubled

classical

Cic. Rep. 2.35: duplicāvit illum prīstinum patrum numerum
Verg. E. 2.67: sōl crēscentīs dēcēdēns duplicat umbrās

duplicō, duplicāre, duplicāvī, duplicātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive; in the passive, to be doubled, grow twofold

To double a number, a sum or a journey (duplicātō itinere, Caes. B.C. 3.76), and so to increase. In poetry and later prose also to bend double (duplicātō poplite, Verg. A. 12.927), and of words, to repeat (Cic. Or. 135; Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • sōl crēscentīs dēcēdēns duplicat umbrās

    the setting sun doubles the lengthening shadowsVerg. E. 2.67

  • prīncipiō duplicāvit illum prīstinum patrum numerum

    first he doubled the old number of senatorsCic. Rep. 2.35

See also double, increase, multiply.
